topicName: Azure Key Vault, Managed Identities, and Secret Rotation
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Secure Secret Rotation in Azure with Key Vault and Managed Identities"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Managing credentials securely in the cloud is critical for maintaining robust security posture. Hardcoded connection strings and static passwords introduce severe vulnerabilities. This tutorial covers how to implement Azure Key Vault, configure Managed Identities for zero-credential applications, and automate secret rotation using Azure Functions."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An active Azure Subscription."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure CLI installed locally or access via Azure Cloud Shell."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of Azure RBAC and serverless functions."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Step 1: Create an Azure Key Vault"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, create a resource group and provision your Azure Key Vault instance. Ensure soft-delete and purge protection are enabled for compliance."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"az group create --name rg-vault-demo --location eastus
az keyvault create --name kv-demo-secure --resource-group rg-vault-demo --location eastus --enable-rbac-authorization"},{"order":10,"type":"heading","text":"Step 2: Configure a Managed Identity"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a User-Assigned Managed Identity that your application will use to authenticate against Azure Key Vault without managing explicit credentials."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"az identity create --name id-app-demo --resource-group rg-vault-demo"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Assign the Key Vault Secrets User role to the managed identity so it can read secrets at runtime."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"VAULT_ID=$(az keyvault show --name kv-demo-secure --query id --output tsv)
PRINCIPAL_ID=$(az identity show --name id-app-demo --resource-group rg-vault-demo --query principalId --output tsv)
az role assignment create --role "Key Vault Secrets User" --assignee $PRINCIPAL_ID --scope $VAULT_ID"},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"Step 3: Implement Automated Secret Rotation"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Key Vault supports automated rotation using Event Grid and Azure Functions. When a secret nears its expiration date, an event triggers the rotation function to generate a new password, update the backend resource, and update the Key Vault secret."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"az keyvault secret set --vault-name kv-demo-secure --name "DatabasePassword" --value "InitialSecretValue123!""},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure the rotation policy on the secret to automatically rotate every 30 days and send notifications via Event Grid."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"az keyvault secret set-attributes --vault-name kv-demo-secure --name "DatabasePassword" --enabled true --expiry-time "2024-12-31T00:00:00Z"
az keyvault secret rotation-policy update --vault-name kv-demo-secure --name "DatabasePassword" --value file://rotation_policy.json"},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Azure Key Vault, Managed Identities, and automated rotation policies, you drastically reduce the blast radius of compromised credentials and eliminate hardcoded secrets from your codebase."}]
